newsitem.title: USA: NRC, ConEd to meet on Indian Pt 2 outage.
newsitem.headline: NRC, ConEd to meet on Indian Pt 2 outage.

text.p: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Friday it will meet Wednesday with Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc (ConEd) to discuss the current outage of its Indian Point 2 nuclear power unit.
"It's scheduled for February 19 at 0930 (EST). We asked them to look at the root cause (to the outage) before restarting," said a NRC spokeswoman.
The meeting is a key step required by the NRC before ConEd can restart the 975 megawatt (MW) Indian Point unit.
In its Friday daily plant report, NRC said Indian Point 2 is expected to startup Saturday February 23.

The spokeswoman said NRC and ConEd will review the company's findings and explain the corrective actions taken during the shutdown of Indian Point 2, as required by a NRC notice sent to ConEd earlier this month.
Indian Point 2, along the Hudson River north of New York City, was shut January 27 to correct problems that caused the feedwater valve to become inoperable.
Subsequent investigations by ConEd pointed to debris in the unit's feedwater and condensate systems as the culprit behind the valve problem, the NRC spokeswoman said.
ConEd also discovered debris in the systems in June 1995, she added.
